newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Building seen improving yr profit.
newsitem.headline: FCL Building seen improving yr profit.

text.p: Fletcher Building is expected to post a modest gain in annual net earnings when it reports next week, but analysts said on Friday the company faced better prospects in the 1997/8 year.
Most expect the division to report a reasonable improvement on its annual profit of NZ$121 million for the June 1996 year but there should be fewer abnormal losses this time around.
Concrete, steel, building products and distribution, and construction and housing divisions were likely put in reasonable contributions.

But within the building products and distribution arms, continued low international prices and a strong New Zealand dollar over the fiscal year were likely to have an impact on returns from medium density fibreboard (MDF).
Distribution and New Zealand construction would be down on the previous year's result, but that previous year had seen the completion of some big projects.

"The plus will be that they have been making progress in exiting some of those overseas construction businesses, so the losses from those will be less than they were last year," David Stanley at Doyle Paterson Brown said.
Guy Hallwright at First NZ Capital said he expected net earnings to come in at around NZ$125-130 million.
In general terms, the outlook would appear reasonably strong, he said.
"The residential outlook might not be that flash, given that we've got a flattish looking economy and higher interest rates," Hallwright said.
"But there is quite a lot of infrastructure work still ahead, with government and local authority spending expected to increase over the next few years," he said.
Fletcher Building, which last traded at NZ$4.30, is due to report on Wednesday.
